page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-standard-4 is a virtual machine instance within the Network Optimized machine family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs built on the x86_64 processor architecture alongside 15.0 GB of system memory, providing an allocation of 3.75 GB of RAM per virtual CPU core. The instance does not include discrete hardware accelerators, registering 0 GPUs, and offers no integrated local storage volumes.

Because the server includes no local disk space, all persistent data storage and operating system requirements must rely on external storage services. The platform also provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, which requires network traffic management through dedicated VPC routing or separate IP allocations. With dedicated CPU core allocation, the hardware provides isolated processing execution free from shared-core contention.

From a cost-efficiency and deployment perspective, c4n-standard-4 offers a standard resource profile with a balanced compute-to-memory ratio. It serves environments that require predictable dedicated execution threads without requiring high memory density or GPU processing. Appropriate operational use cases include network-focused services, API backends, containerized microservices, and general compute workloads that decouple state to external databases.

This provides an allocation of 3.75 GB of RAM per virtual processor, presenting a balanced hardware footprint. Because processing cores are dedicated rather than shared or burstable, compute cycles maintain predictable performance without resource contention from adjacent tenants. The c4n-standard-4 instance is structured for network-oriented workloads, mid-tier application tiers, API gateways, and microservices that operate effectively with decoupled persistent storage.
